Title: Ireland – Education and training services – Communication & Online Learning Enhancement & Scientific Advisory (UCC-VEAT-2024-07)
Procedure title: Communication & Online Learning Enhancement & Scientific Advisory (UCC-VEAT-2024-07)
Description: This is a voluntary ex-ante transparency (VEAT) notice. It acknowledges that University College Cork (UCC) contracted with Stichting Climate-KIC International Foundation (Climate-KIC), for the provision of support and leadership of online and in-person training event implementation for the Copernicus Atmospheric Monitoring Service and Copernicus Climate Change Service, under the competitively won ECMWF Service Contract CJS2_156b_UCC. Under CJS2_156b_UCC, UCC is leading a Service team to provide support to the ECMWF in implementing training events and online learning resources for the two Copernicus Services. Climate-KIC will lead the event implementation activities for the overall Service contract, and contribute to the Scientific Advisory Committee. Climate-KIC were uniquely placed in terms of skillsets, professional networks and relationships to perform their role in this overall service contract, further enhanced by their good standing, and track record of excellence. They brought their extensive networks in the worlds of business, academia, and the public and non-profit sectors into the Service team. For example, Climate-KIC are an official member of the Copernicus Academy since 2018 which has equipped them with an exceptional insight into the educational and training landscape of the Copernicus Programme - a critical requirement for this work. In addition, Climate-KIC is already active across Europe and online, running a range of inspirational education programmes for students, postgraduates, and professionals. This is in alignment with the requirements of the Service contract, specifically in delivering high-quality, customised Training events for the 2 Copernicus Services (Atmospheric and Climate) operated by the ECMWF. Within their staff, Climate-KIC also had the required expertise in event management, professional networks, Copernicus activities, Copernicus product uses, and product & service development that was needed for the Service’s Scientific Advisory Committee - a key Quality Control mechanism embedded within the contract Service – in addition to their highly beneficial professional networks. This is in close alignment with the requirements of the overarching Service contract between UCC and the ECMWF, specifically to deliver high-quality, customised online and in-person training events that are quality controlled to a standard of high scientific and professional rigour. The company was therefore selected to participate in the bid for the CJS2_156b ITT as their unique combination of skillsets, technical expertise, capabilities and networks complemented those of the bidding consortium, completing it’s offering to the ECMWF. They were integral to the awarded bid, and have been contracted accordingly.

Procedure title: In-person and online training expertise, scientific advisory (UCC-VEAT-2024-04)
Description: This is a voluntary ex-ante transparency (VEAT) notice. It acknowledges that University College Cork contracted with Collecte Localisation Satellites (CLS), for the provision of support of online learning resource development and enhancement, training expertise and scientific oversight for the Copernicus Atmospheric Monitoring Service and Copernicus Climate Change Service, under the competitively won ECMWF Service Contract CJS2_156b_UCC. Under CJS2_156b_UCC, UCC is leading a Service team to provide support to the ECMWF in implementing training events and online learning resources for the two Copernicus Services. CLS will (i) support the online learning resource activities for the overall Service contract, providing technical support to implement resource solutions, (ii) contribute to the Scientific Advisory Committee, and (iii) support Training event implementation. CLS were uniquely placed in terms of skillsets, professional networks and relationships to perform their role in this overall service contract, further enhanced by their good standing, and track record of excellence. They have extensive experience in developing integrated offers to a broad range of Service-relevant stakeholders including: government, industry and the scientific community and services, in sectors such as Environment & climate monitoring, Mobility, Energy & infrastructures, amongst others. They have a dedicated team of data scientists who work closely with oceanographers to develop new methodologies, understandings and ocean science communications. They have coupled this with a growing, and impressive training portfolio in Earth Observation applications - critical to the Copernicus programme – and are existing suppliers of data and training materials to the Copernicus Climate Service, and Copernicus Marine Service (in addition to ESA, CNES and many other global partners, which brought considerable potential for synergies to the Service). CLS have also delivered staff training programmes to field and IT operators and end-users, while having also developed a full Moodle course for EUMETSAT, and a range of Jupyter applications and notebooks, the bedrock of the ECMWF's online training offering. Their staff are experienced in delivering in-person training on ocean scient topics such as altimetry, a key area for capacity building in the Copernicus community. In addition, they bring their oceans experience, training experience and knowledge of satellite systems to satisfy a critical niche for expertise in the Service’s Scientific Advisory Committee - a key Quality Control mechanism embedded within the contract Service. This is in close alignment with the requirements of the overarching Service contract between UCC and the ECMWF, specifically to deliver high-quality, customised training and developing learning resources for Copernicus services that are quality controlled to a standard of high scientific rigour. The company was therefore selected to participate in the bid for the CJS2_156b ITT as their unique combination of skillsets, technical expertise, capabilities and networks complemented those of the bidding consortium, completing it’s offering to the ECMWF. They were integral to the awarded bid, and have been contracted accordingly.

It acknowledges that University College Cork (UCC) contracted with Universidad de Málaga (UMA), for the provision of support in Scientific Advisory, online learning resource enhancement, and online & in-person training for the Copernicus Atmospheric Monitoring Service and Copernicus Climate Change Service, under the competitively won ECMWF Service Contract CJS2_156b_UCC. Under CJS2_156b_UCC, UCC is leading a Service team to provide support to the ECMWF in implementing training events and online learning resources for the two Copernicus Services. UMA will contribute to the Scientific Advisory Committee, online learning resource, and training event activities for the overall Service contract, providing niche technical, expertise and scientific oversight support. UMA were uniquely placed in terms of skillsets, professional networks and relationships to perform their role in this overall service contract, further enhanced by their good standing, and track record of excellence. They brought the international European Topic Centre for Spatial Analysis and Synthesis (ETC-UMA) into the Service Contract, where environmental knowledge to support evidence-based policy and decision-making at different scales is developed, supported by the work of the Khaos research group, specialised in Big Data analytics, machine learning and artificial intelligence - all of which are quickly growing topics of interest to Copernicus trainees. The ETC-UMA team have thematic skills and perspectives of high importance to the training topics the Service is expected to advise on, including environmental remote sensing, geospatial data management and publication, indicator development, ecosystems and services assessments of marine and terrestrial environments. Additionally, researchers at ETC-UMA are currently part of the core team of the European Topic Centre on Data Integration and Digitalisation (ETC/DI) supporting the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service. UMA leads on their user uptake initiatives to promote the service portfolio within the European Environment Agency, among the other ETCs and Commission Services (such as DG Agri, Eurostat, etc.), and supports stakeholder engagement at Member State level through preparing capacity building material and workshop design. As a university, UMA is a key contributor of training experience, enhanced by organising Copernicus Hackathons, their connections within the Copernicus community, and their founding role in the Copernicus Academy. As such, they bring the skills, expertise, networks, good standing and track record to meet the needs of the Service's Scientific Advisory Committee, Training Event implementation, and Online training resource development. This is in close alignment with the requirements of the overarching Service contract between UCC and the ECMWF, specifically to deliver high-quality, customised training and developing learning resources for Copernicus services that are quality controlled to a standard of high scientific rigour. The institute was therefore selected to participate in the bid for the CJS2_156b ITT as their unique combination of skillsets, technical expertise, capabilities and networks complemented those of the bidding consortium, completing it’s offering to the ECMWF. They were integral to the awarded bid, and have been contracted accordingly.

Title: Ireland – Engineering works and construction works – Darndale Park – waste removal and wall construction
Procedure title: Darndale Park – waste removal and wall construction
Description: The Contract comprises clearance and removal of approximately 40,000 tonnes of illegally dumped waste material and construction of boundary treatments and 117m of new 2.5m high precast boundary wall and footpath between Darndale Park and a group of Traveller Accommodation site known as the Northern Sites on the north side of Dublin within the boundaries of Darndale and Priorswood. The works shall include site clearance, removal of all waste material (investigations suggest non-hazardous), removal of asbestos, removal of end-of-life vehicles and other electrical goods, treatment and removal of invasive species, construction of concrete boundary walls, construction of new footpath, environmental monitoring. There is a requirement for removal of hazardous waste should it be encountered. Temporary works shall include construction of a construction stage haul road through Darndale Park to provide site access and all associated reinstatement works, protection to all existing services, fencing of works areas etc. Design of temporary works shall form part of the works. The estimated value of the works is envisaged to be €7.5m (ex VAT) however this figure will largely be dependent on the make-up of the waste material. Applications are only sought from Contractors who have a proven track record in the works as described above. Applications are not sought from general building contractors who proposed to sub-contract the whole of the works.. Please note that this project is subject to funding. Title: Ireland – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Covid 19 Vaccination System expansion
Procedure title: Covid 19 Vaccination System expansion
Description: In December 2020, the HSE procured a solution under Emergency Procurement Regulation 32 to support the response to the Covid 19 Immunisation programme. The solution was built on Salesforce CRM platform and provided an immunisation system (Covax) and a public facing support platform (Service Cloud). Due to the extended duration of the pandemic, the ongoing need for comprehensive vaccination management, and a changing patient care pathway, continued integration and expansion of the solution was required to meet Public Health requirements. Covax has undergone significant development over three years, evolving from a MVP into a comprehensive immunisation system capable of managing multiple vaccine types. Covax vaccination platform has evolved to support the following: patient account creation; vaccination recording; full patient vaccination histories; administration of multiple vaccine products; configurable interval times and doses; configurable risk factors; product-based eligibility criteria; adverse reaction capabilities; diverse vaccine administration locations. Additional functionality includes patient portal; appointment scheduling; reporting and analytics; user training platform; support platform; communication platform. With Covax embedded as the core, a network of interconnected software applications, data repositories, integration points, platforms and services have been built up to create the comprehensive and mature national immunisation ecosystem which is in use today. Vaccination records are ingested into Covax from GPs, Pharmacies, and various Community organisations. Data is enriched on Covax through integration with IHI, GP registry, Eircode, and a vaccination asset management system. National vaccination reporting is enabled though integration with the HSE’s data lake. Covax is an established and embedded cornerstone of the national IT infrastructure. It is currently the largest patient database in the HSE, with over 4.4 million patient records and over 16 million recorded vaccinations. The architecture of the Covax system is proven in terms of both performance and scale, with the recording of 400,000 vaccinations per week at peak. The Covax public-facing portal has facilitated the self-registration of 2.2 million patients for vaccination to date and appointment scheduling functionality has created over 7.5 million appointments. Since 2021, Covax has ingested over 6 million vaccination records from GPs and 2 million from pharmacies. To date, over 20,000 clinical and operational staff have been trained to use the Covax system. Embedded in the pandemic response was the requirement for HSE Live to provide public-facing support. Salesforce Service Cloud was used to provide this support, and with extensive and incremental development, this generic platform was tailored for use by multiple Covid support teams across the HSE including HSE Live, DCC team, HSE NSD (National Service Desk), Covax support and GP Resolver teams.
Lot description: In December 2020 the HSE procured a solution under Emergency Procurement Regulation 32 to support the response to the Covid 19 Immunisation programme. Salesforce licenses were procured initially for the vaccination management programme. The solution was built on Salesforce CRM platform and provided an immunisation system (Covax) and a public facing support platform (Service Cloud). Due to the extended duration of the pandemic, the changing patient care pathway and the ongoing need to support a post pandemic covid vaccination regime, continued integration and expansion to meet Public Health requirements was necessary. The solution has undergone significant development over three years, evolving from a minimum viable product into a comprehensive immunisation system capable of managing multiple vaccine types. A network of interconnected software applications, data repositories, integration points, platforms and services have been built up to create a complex and mature Immunisation Ecosystem with Covax at its core. The capability to extend Covax to meet the requirements for other immunisation programmes, such as Flu and Pneumococcal, has already been delivered and proven. Covax is now an embedded component of the national IT infrastructure used to record Covid, Influenza (Flu), and Pneumococcal vaccinations. It is currently the largest patient database in the HSE, with 4.4 million patient records and over 16 million recorded vaccinations. The HSE now intends to progress with the addition of further vaccinations leading to Covax becoming the National Immunisation Information System (NIIS). The technical sophistication and richness of the current immunisation ecosystem make it the ideal basis from which to fulfil NIIS requirements with minimal adaptation, in a timely and cost-effective manner, while avoiding duplication of existing efforts and mitigating the current clinical risks. The HSE intends to move forward as follows: - Extend the use of the Covax system to support the administration of the National Immunisation programmes - Extend the use of Service Cloud to support all HSELive communication services - Broaden the use of Salesforce CRM functionality to include other services as required This will be done through the establishment of a Dynamic Purchasing System arrangement for ongoing products and services. To ensure continuity of safe delivery of health services and a value for money return on the significant capital investment to date, the HSE will continue with the current arrangements until the new arrangement is established.

Title: Ireland – Repair and maintenance services of precision equipment – Request for Tenders for the provision of maintenance services for Met Eireann’s meteorological and environmental monitoring instrumentation and related infrastructure.
Procedure title: Request for Tenders for the provision of maintenance services for Met Eireann’s meteorological and environmental monitoring instrumentation and related infrastructure.
Description: Met Éireann’s maintains a national network of automated climatological stations, which are referred to as CAMP network stations. The information from these sensors are recorded, stored and transmitted, utilising data loggers and associated communication equipment, to Met Éireann HQ, for input into the Met Éireann database. This tender relates to the provision of regular scheduled maintenance to these stations. The CAMP (Climate) network consists of 78 stations currently (this number is projected to increase to 81) located throughout the country, on a mixture of private and public land. Scheduled maintenance is completed on a 2 year rotational basis with approximately 40 sites being visited each year. All maintenance must be completed with adherence to the current WMO guidance , including, if acceptable, any amendment or update to same. Applicant should refer to https://wmo.int/about-us/governance/technical-commissions/standards-and-recommended-practices for the most recent publication. The tendering company will undertake, at a minimum, one scheduled maintenance visit to each site location every 2 year period, fulfilling the agreed requirements. The sites are grouped by region (see Site Regional Map in the Tender documentation) and the work schedule is normally planned to reflect this, However, if several issues occur at a particular station, then the scheduled maintenance for that particular site may be brought forward on occasion. Urgent, non scheduled maintenance may also be required on occasion to any of the network stations. The tenderer is invited to include, on a per station basis, a quotation for this work.

Title: Ireland – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Mobile Data Collection Platform.
Procedure title: Mobile Data Collection Platform.
Description: Iarnród Éireann (IÉ) is seeking a partner to implement a range of field work management applications with a data collection system at its core. It is planned to implement the system with approximately 500 users, initially. The core system will link to SAP, SharePoint and other IT systems using a-synchronous connections (via API), and will initially be focused on 6 elements: i. Work Order Management Application; ii. Data Collection Tools; iii. Form Creation; iv. Lone Work Systems; v. GIS and GPS Navigation System; vi. Service Level Agreement. IÉ requires that this Mobile Data Collection Platform will be flexible enough to be applied to a number of field data collection business processes in various areas of the organisation.The current contract with AMT Sybex is set to expire on January 22, 2025. At tender stage in 2017 it was considered that a seven-year term would be sufficient as it was anticipated that the mobile data collection functionality would be incorporated into other enterprise-wide systems during the term of the contract, negating the need for a separate standalone platform. However, while it is still intended to incorporate this functionality into a separate enterprise solution (e.g. as part of the proposed SAP upgrade), since this system is core to the IÉ Asset Management System and is also utilised by IÉ Safety Teams across the organisation, continuity of service is required. The integration of Fieldreach into IÉ's operations has been extensive, with the platform being deeply embedded in engineering workflows and asset management activities. Transitioning to a new provider at this stage would introduce significant technical and economic challenges: • Technical Complexity and Integration Costs: The integration of Fieldreach with IÉ’s SAP ECC system and other critical business processes was a highly customized and iterative process. A new provider would necessitate substantial redevelopment and re-integration, leading to high costs and potential disruptions in service. If a new system was to be procured, an alternative integration layer between SAP and the new tool would have to be designed, built and tested. This would require resources from GITT, IÉ technical staff and a third party integration partner. It is anticipated that the costs associated with these works would be in the region of €1M (excl. VAT). Further additional duplication of costs and risk would be incurred by transferring data from the current suppliers’ servers to those of a new supplier. • Operational Disruption: Adopting a new platform would require extensive retraining of approximately 800 users. This transition period could significantly impact productivity and the efficiency of our maintenance and asset management activities, risking compliance and operational integrity. On the basis of the above and based on the substantial technical and economic implications, IÉ is seeking approval to conclude negotiations with AMT Sybex with a view to extending the term of this contract for a further period of up to 5 years up to January 2030, during which, it is anticipated the platform will be phased out as IÉ transitions to another enterprise solution. By extending the contract with AMT Sybex, IÉ can ensure the continuity of critical asset management operations, avoid unnecessary disruptions, and maintain operational efficiency. The continuation of the current platform will facilitate a seamless workflow for our staff and uphold the standards of our asset management processes.

Title: Ireland – Miscellaneous spare parts – Bus Éireann Vehicle Spare Parts Qualification Panel
Procedure title: Bus Éireann Vehicle Spare Parts Qualification Panel
Description: Bus Éireann proposes establishing a Vehicle Spare Parts Qualification panels of potential suppliers which will be maintained for a period of eight (8) years from the date of establishment, unless terminated earlier by the Contracting Authority. The Qualification Panels will be established in respect to different parts categories as set out below. Applicants may apply for one or more Panels. Panel 1 - Supply of, Repair and Maintenance for Body Parts Panel 2 - Supply of Parts, Repair and Maintenance of Chassis Panel 3 - Supply of Parts, Repair and Maintenance of Body Panels and Structure Panel 4 - Supply of Parts, Repair and Maintenance of Glazing Panel 5 - Supply of Parts, Repair and Maintenance of Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning Systems Panel 6 - Supply of, Repair and Maintenance of Hoses and Pipes Panel 7 - Supply of, Repair and Maintenance of Exterior and Interior Fittings Panel 8 - Supply of, Repair and Maintenance of Ancillary Onboard Equipment Panel 9 - Supply of Tyres and Wheels Panel 10 - Supply of Parts to, Repairs and Maintenance of Braking Systems Panel 11 - Supply of, Repair and Maintenance of Suspension and Steering Systems Panel 12 - Supply of, Repair and Maintenance for General Driveline Systems Panel 13 – Supply of Filters Panel 14 - Supply of, Repair and Maintenance of Electrical and Electronic Components Panel 15 - Supply of Miscellaneous Electric or Electronic Components Panel 16 - Supply of Miscellaneous Mechanical or Electronic Components Successful applicants will form part of the Qualification Panel. Being on the Qualification Panel does not give the supplier any guarantee of work but may enable the supplier to tender for framework agreements, and contracts for individual projects, to be set up through the Qualification Panel from time to time. When a competition for a particular framework agreement or contract from the Qualification Panel is required, registered applicants may be taken through a further pre-qualification process to determine those to be invited to tender or negotiate. Turnover will be used to determine which Panel member(s) will be invited to tender based on the overall value of the framework agreement or contract. When determining which companies will be invited to tender, only those with a turnover of twice the annual value of the contract will be invited. Applicants who have been deemed suitably qualified may be invited to submit a formal tender for the requirements that arise during the Qualification Panel term. This Notice does not prevent the Contracting Authority from issuing other contract notices for specific requirements from time to time, including procurements outside the Qualification Panel for requirements falling within the scope of the Qualification Panel.

Procedure title: Award of Contract to Breffni Group Ltd. for Waste Removal and Wall Construction in Darndale Park
Description: Dublin City Council has awarded a contract to Breffni Group Ltd. The Contract comprises clearance and removal of approximately 40,000 tonnes of illegally dumped waste material and construction of boundary treatments and 117m of new 2.5m high precast boundary wall and footpath between Darndale Park and a group of Traveller Accommodation site known as the Northern Sites on the north side of Dublin within the boundaries of Darndale and Priorswood. The works shall include site clearance, removal of all waste material (investigations suggest non-hazardous), removal of asbestos, removal of end-of-life vehicles and other electrical goods, treatment and removal of invasive species, construction of concrete boundary walls, construction of new footpath, environmental monitoring. There is a requirement for removal of hazardous waste should it be encountered. Temporary works shall include construction of a construction stage haul road through Darndale Park to provide site access and all associated reinstatement works, protection to all existing services, fencing of works areas etc. Design of temporary works shall form part of the works.

Title: Ireland – Demolition, site preparation and clearance work – TII390_M110_Enabling Works and Specialist Heritage Works Framework for MetroLink
Procedure title: TII390_M110_Enabling Works and Specialist Heritage Works Framework for MetroLink
Description: MetroLink will provide a high speed, high capacity, high frequency, modern and efficient public transport service for passengers travelling along the Swords/Airport to City Centre corridor in Dublin, which will be capable of integration with other modes of public transport. Further information on MetroLink is available at www.metrolink.ie/ In advance of the MetroLink main infrastructure works contracts, TII will commence the procurement of the Enabling Works Programme. The Enabling Works Programme comprises the establishment of a suite of framework agreements and qualification systems select contractors to deliver enabling works which will commence in advance of the main infrastructure works contracts (in respect of civil engineering, tunnelling and station works). The enabling works will include the removal and/or relocation of existing utilities, archaeology, heritage items (for storage/replacement) and buildings from site and undertaking other survey activities. To deliver the enabling and advance works for MetroLink, TII intends to establish 3 no. multi-party framework agreements as listed below each through a negotiated procedure with a prior call for competition. • Enabling Works and Specialist Heritage Works Framework; • Utilities Framework; and • Civils Enabling Works Framework. TII also intends to establish a qualification system for independent environmental monitoring and a qualification system for archaeology services as part of the Enabling Works Programme. The proposed duration of the framework agreements is 8 years with an option to extend for 4 years to facilitate the procurement of any associated works that may be required over the duration of the Frameworks. This PIN is in connection with the Enabling Works and Specialist Heritage Works Framework. The purpose of this PIN is to alert the market to TII’s intention to undertake market consultation and subsequently commence a procurement in Q3 2025. It is anticipated that the prequalification documentation will be issued in Q3 2025 with the instructions to tenderers issued in Q4 2025 or Q1 2026. TII intends to utilise the NEC4 Engineering Construction Contract (ECC) form of contracts for call offs placed under this framework. Interested parties can register their interest at https://www.etenders.gov.ie Any interested parties wishing to respond to the market consultation in advance of procurement commencement, are required to send a request to the following email address supplychainmetrolink@tii.ie by 12:00hrs on the 23rd May 2025 seeking to be issued with a copy of the briefing pack for review and completion of the questionnaire contained within the pack. The questionnaire is required to be completed in full and returned by the closing date of the 27th May 2025 by 12:00hrs to the following email address supplychainmetrolink@tii.ie. Following receipt of completed questionnaires from interested parties, TII proposes to invite selected participants to provide further information by way of one-to-one clarification meetings to be held on the 3rd , 4th and 5th June 2025. To be deemed an interested party you must register your interest on supplychainmetrolink@tii.ie. TII intends to hold a webinar for the registered interested parties in relation to this procurement on May 29th 2025 at 12:00hrs. TII previously issued a PIN in connection with the MetroLink Advance Works packages for market consultation (reference OJ S 217/2023 10/11/2023)

Title: Ireland – Construction work for bridges and tunnels, shafts and subways – Global PIN for the MetroLink programme related to: • Programme Delivery Partner (PDP) Contract. • M401/402 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts. • M500 Contract (DBFOM).
Procedure title: Global PIN for the MetroLink programme related to: • Programme Delivery Partner (PDP) Contract. • M401/402 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts. • M500 Contract (DBFOM).
Description: MetroLink will provide a high speed, high capacity, high frequency, modern and efficient public transport service for passengers travelling along the Swords/Airport to City Centre corridor in Dublin, which will be capable of integration with other modes of public transport. Further information on MetroLink is available at www.metrolink.ie MetroLink will be procured under a series of public works and services contracts: Programme Delivery Partner (“PDP”) Contract: The PDP Contract shall support Transport Infrastructure Ireland (“TII”) through providing capability and capacity to support the TII organisational structure in post-contract, construction and delivery (including contract management functions such as fulfilling role of “Project Manager” and “Supervisor” under the M401/M402 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts and performance of the statutory function of Project Supervisor Construction Stage under the M401/M402 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts and the M500 Contract). M401/402 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts: Two NEC4 Engineering and Construction Contract (ECC) contracts will be let for the civil engineering and infrastructure works including track alignment preparation, stations and structures including bridges and tunnels. Further detail on the scope of the two M400 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts is as envisaged below: 1. Southern Section M401 – Charlemont to Northwood: • Bored tunnels and portals, evacuation / intervention shafts; and • Below ground station excavations at Charlemont, St Stephen’s Green, Tara, O’Connell, Mater, Glasnevin, Griffith Park, Collins Avenue, Ballymun, Northwood up to 35m deep including shell and core structures. 2. Northern Section M402 - Northwood to Estuary: • M50 viaduct, surface route (retained cut, cut and cover) and at-grade sections; • Broadmeadow river viaduct; • Estuary Station Park and Ride Facility (bulk earthworks and site preparation); • Preparation of the Dardistown Depot site and access road; • Bored tunnels and portals, evacuation / intervention shafts; and • Stations excavations and associated logistics including Dardistown, Dublin Airport, Fosterstown, Swords Central, Seatown and Estuary. M500 Contract An availability-based design, build, finance, operate and maintain (“DBFOM”) contract to appoint a project company (“M500 Contractor”) who will carry out design and construction, raise finance in respect of such construction, and subsequently provide the integrated operation and maintenance of the public passenger transport service. The M500 Contractor will be responsible for the design, manufacture, supply and installation of the metro rolling stock, signalling system (at Grade of Operation 4 – an automated railway), a railway depot and maintenance facility, metro control centre building(s) together with the installation of all line-wide trackwork, overhead contact system, power and communication systems, mechanical and electrical systems including tunnel and station ventilation, people movement systems and the fit out and finishes in sixteen stations plus urban realm works. The M500 Contractor will be required to procure financing in respect of the abovementioned works, and following completion of the works, the M500 Contractor will be responsible for the operation and maintenance of the MetroLink system as a whole. TII proposes to award an Early Services Agreement to the preferred tenderer for the M500 Contract, pursuant to which the preferred tenderer will be required to provide early services related to, inter alia, railway systems integration prior to financial close. In advance of the award of the M400 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts and the M500 Contract, TII intends to award a series of enabling works framework agreements (the “M100 Contracts”) and a DPS purchasing system to deliver enabling works to include the removal and/or relocation of existing utilities, archaeology, heritage items (for storage/replacement) and buildings from site and undertaking other monitoring and survey activities. Separate Periodic Notices were published for the M100 Contracts on 19th May 2025: • Civils Enabling Works Framework TED Reference: 320539-2025 - Planning • Utilities Framework TED Reference: 319450-2025 - Planning • Enabling Works and Specialist Heritage Works Framework TED Reference: 321121-2025 - Planning • Independent Monitoring and Surveying Qualification System TED Reference: 321586-2025 - Planning • Archaeology Services Qualification System TED Reference: 321984-2025 - Planning This Global PIN is further to other previous publications concerning this project including: • TED Reference: 518372-2024, released on 29 of August 2024, related to the M400 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts. • TED Reference: 509146-2024, released on 26 August 2024, related to the PDP Contract. • TED Reference: 557522-2023, released on 15 September 2023, related to the M500 Contract. • TED Reference: 208843-2022, released on 19 April 2022, related to the M500 Contract. • TED Reference: 536230-2019, released on 12 November 2019, related to MetroLink as a whole.

Title: Ireland – Construction work – 9165 Single Supplier Framework Agreement for Design and Build Signalling and Telecoms Contractor for DART +
Procedure title: 9165 Single Supplier Framework Agreement for Design and Build Signalling and Telecoms Contractor for DART +
Description: Iarnród Éireann (IÉ) has an existing contract in place for the Long-Term Supply, Installation, Testing, and Commissioning of a Computer-Based Interlocking System (CBIS). As part of the DART+ Programme, IÉ is seeking to appoint an experienced contractor to the DART+ Single Supplier Framework for Design & Build Signalling & Telecoms. The appointed contractor will be responsible for the design, construction, and commissioning of all Signalling and Telecoms works, with the exception of those tasks specifically designated as the responsibility of the interlocking system OEM (Original Equipment manufacturer).For the avoidance of doubt, this framework excludes interlocking system OEM works, which will continue to be delivered under IÉ’s existing CBIS Framework. The DART+ Single Supplier Framework for Design & Build Signalling & Telecoms will include the detailed design, installation, testing and commissioning (as appropriate) of the following: • A new signalling system, including lineside signals, lineside equipment housings, train detection equipment, balise installation, point operating equipment and all associated cabling. • ETCS Level 1 train protection system, designed and provided by the CBI framework supplier, will be installed and commissioned by the appointed S&T Contractor • Alterations as required where the new signalling systems will fringe to existing signalling systems. • Power supply and distribution systems to support S&T equipment, including signalling & telecoms power supply systems. • Points heating systems. • Telecoms systems (including both fibre and copper cabling) to support the signalling system. • Lineside telephones. • The decommissioning of existing level crossings, including the recovery of existing equipment. • The decommissioning and recovery of redundant signalling & telecoms systems and electrical systems. • Ancillary systems for lineside buildings and equipment housings, including lighting, cable management, telecoms connections, environmental control, fire detection and suppression systems, access control and intruder alarm systems. • Collaborating with and supporting, as required, the IÉ appointed Maintainer of the National Traffic Control Centre (NTCC), who will undertake required upgrades to systems (including the Traffic management System) within the NTCC. Similarly, the project shall interface the with existing Connolly Train Control (CTC) centre. Where any existing system is to be retained, immunisation works as required to enable the introduction of overhead Electrification (by others). • Provision of training material to support the briefing and training of drivers, signallers and other operational staff.
Lot description: This is a call to competition by IE for the procurement of a Design and Build Signalling and Telecoms Contractor by way of a single supplier Framework Agreement, one Contractor will be the sole supplier. DART+ is a transformative programme of projects that aims to modernise and improve existing rail services in the Greater Dublin Area (GDA). The DART network will increase from 50 kilometres to 150 kilometres transforming commuter train travel in the Greater Dublin Area. It will provide a sustainable, electrified, reliable and more frequent rail service improving capacity in all rail corridors serving Dublin, bringing DART travel with all its benefits to new and existing communities. The provision of a new electrified fleet will improve capacity and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

Procedure title: Request for Tender for Health and Safety Consultancy Services (PSCS) at MEDITE Europe DAC ‘25
Description: MEDITE Europe DAC are seeking suitably qualified companies for the supply of PSCS services to support the shortly commencing construction phase of Project Shine. Please see Project Supervisor Construction Stage (PSCS) services outlined below We have plans to modernize our MDF facility with an investment in new equipment called Project Shine. 3D layout of existing + proposed can be found in Appendix 3: Layout Drawings. (Which can be made available upon request to Ciara.Walsh@mdfosb.com following signing an NDA). Project Shine involves the installation of the following: • Wet fuel handling system of which the main component are: • Walking floor system • Various conveyors • Screens + Hoppers • Dry Fuel handling system of which the main components are: • Edge trim + dust silo • Blowers • Ducting and diverters • Energy plant of which the main components are: • Walking floor system for biomass fuel • Main 56MW biomass furnace • Thermal Oil Heating + pumping • Electrostatic Precipitator • Steam Generator • Associated ID fans: recirculation, primary + secondary. • MDF dryers of which the main components are: • Hot Gas Duct • Face Dryer • Core Dryer • Associated fans • Services + utilities to the above, mainly: • Thermal oil • Compressed air • Process Water • Fire detection + suppression • Natural Gas • Steam • Storm and foul water • Bunds where necessary The main requirements of the PSCS Services are outlined below • Organise effective co-operation, co-ordination + communication between contractors, sub-contractors + client through daily whiteboard, weekly + monthly meetings • Liaise with the various vendors/contractors, identify hazards arising from the construction or from the technical, organisational, planning or time related aspects of the project. Review of proposed equipment layouts and vendor tender documents for necessary health + safety requirements. Make recommendations to client + contractors. • Where possible, eliminate the hazards or reduce the risks through consultation + co-operation of and between contractors and client. Identify interdependencies and possible clashes between various vendor packages so they can be resolved in a timely manner. • Communicate necessary control measures, design assumptions or remaining risks to the contractors so they can be dealt with. • Review Vendor Proposals for compliance with EU Machinery Directive + ATEX requirements. • Ensure all HAZOP recommendations are implemented. • Review Building design layout for compliance with relevant safety regulations and best. (BCAR etc.) • Complete AF2 forms and all other necessary notices + communications to H.S.A. • Complete the Health + Safety Plan (including traffic management plan, walkways, construction compound, laydown areas). • Appoint a safety adviser where there are more than 100 personnel on site • Provide all necessary Safety File information to the PSDP. • Ensure there is adequate Welfare facilities for number of personnel. • Manage the segregation and restricted entry to the construction site • Responsible for Inductions • Maintain registers + records for: • Training files • Safe pass • CSCS • Harness training • First aid • PAT equipment • GA1 Report of Thorough Examination • GA2 Weekly Examination of Lifting Equipment • GA3 Work Equipment for Working at Height • Accidents + incidents • Dangerous Occurrences • Toolbox talks • Relevant topics to be covered • Records • Evacuation drills • Safety equipment inspections i.e. harness • Issue + close Permit to Works not limited to; • Working at Height • LOTO • Confined Space • Define Hot Work Areas + implement permits • NDT X-ray • Permits outside of main construction site/client areas • Sprinkler impairments ** Please find the attached Tender Document for the full and complete Scope of Works

Title: Ireland – Alarm-monitoring services – Provision of Lone Worker Devices and a Response Centre
Procedure title: Provision of Lone Worker Devices and a Response Centre
Description: The device must be robust enough to withstand normal wear and tear in an industrial environment. The device must be lightweight, portable and must include a holder to carry the device on your person, easily accessible and CE compliant. A sample device must be provided to examine these features with tender. The device must be water resistant (e.g. IP67). The device must have a minimum 50 hour plus duration of battery life in normal operational use per single charge. Easily activated SOS button to request assistance 2-way speaker communication following alarm activation GPS positioning with alert delivery over 2/3/4G The solution must be end to end and must operate independently of the Council’s own ICT infrastructure Fall/Man Down alarm functionality - activation capability (can be turned on/off) should be included. Functionality should provide for an event including falls or sudden impact. Capability for the response Centre to let the user know they are listening (discretely and otherwise). Access to a 24-hour response Centre licensed by the Private Security Authority (PSA) for dealing with alarms. Please supply one (1) proposed device with tender response document. Tenderers must provide training for Wexford County Council staff in Council Offices on award of contract. Please note tender price for devices should include the cost of training. The Tenderer will be required to provide monthly information to the Health and Safety Section at Wexford County Council Offices to discuss: Contract performance; Use of device; Training needs; Incident reviews; Invoicing details; Service satisfaction. Please note a monthly email is required outlining incidents in previous month. The Tenderer will be required to outline the lone working system administration requirements. Preference given to tenders minimizing end user administration for Wexford County Council.

Title: Ireland – Construction work for gas pipelines – 24/033 - Qualification System for the provision of Engineering, Procurement and Construction Services for South West Scotland Onshore System (SWSOS)
Procedure title: 24/033 - Qualification System for the provision of Engineering, Procurement and Construction Services for South West Scotland Onshore System (SWSOS)
Description: GNI and GNI (UK) are seeking experienced EPCS contractors to deliver a series of critical infrastructure upgrades as part of the SWSOS Decarbonisation Programme, a cornerstone of our commitment to achieving Net Zero by 2050. This tender covers multiple work packages, including the design, procurement, construction, and integration of new electric drive compressor halls across operational sites in Scotland. The successful contractor will manage complex interfaces between new and existing assets, ensuring seamless integration of mechanical, electrical, and control systems, while adhering to stringent cybersecurity and safety standards. This initiative represents a strategic investment in sustainable energy infrastructure and offers an opportunity to collaborate on projects of significant scale and impact within a multinational framework. SCOPE OF REQUIREMENTS: The scope of this tender encompasses overall project management and delivery across multiple work packages, including but not limited to the following: Detailed Design Procurement Procurement of detailed design for new compressor halls, based on the GNI suite of functional specifications. Materials Procurement Mechanical materials: high-pressure pipework, valves, and fittings. Electrical materials: interconnecting cabling and junction boxes. Instrumentation materials: transmitters and data cabling. Note: The second-stage tender process (CFC) will confirm the final requirements and clarify the full scope boundaries for the electric motor drive (EMD) package and the contractor’s scope. Construction Activities Construction of new compressor halls. Completion of all civil works, including excavations, foundations, structural steel, compressor foundations, and ancillary electrical buildings. Installation of interconnecting pipework, electrical and control cabling, and junction boxes. Integration and System Tie-ins Integration of new electric drive compressors into the existing fleet of gas turbines. Mechanical, electrical, and control system tie-ins at operational compressor stations across GNI UK sites in Scotland. Security and Cybersecurity Installation of security systems and implementation of cybersecurity controls in line with GNI specifications. Testing and Commissioning Full responsibility for FAT and SAT activities. Commissioning and start-up of all new systems. Additional Scope Notes: GNI may procure electric motor drive (EMD) packages separately. GNI will manage all permitting and planning permissions. GNI will separately upgrade incoming site electrical supply to power the new EMD packages. Indicative EPCS Scope Boundary: The EPCS scope is envisaged to cover all elements required for the delivery of an electric drive compressor station as outlined above. A more detailed scope is provided within the Appendices of the Qualification System Questionnaire documents

Title: Ireland – Construction work – Metrolink vehicle safety features for all construction and logistics activity involving HGV usage during the programme.
Procedure title: Metrolink vehicle safety features for all construction and logistics activity involving HGV usage during the programme.
Description: Metrolink vehicle safety features for all construction and logistics activity involving HGV usage during the programme: • M100 – Advance Works (Land access and clearance, Archaeology, Utilities, environmental monitoring and sewer alignment works). • M300 – Enabling Works (Glasnevin Station, O’Connell Street Station Box, Irish Rail Glasnevin Interface and ESBN HV MV connections). • M400 - Main Civils Works – (M401 Civil Works Southern Section, M402 Civil Works Northern Section). • M500 – DBFOM (Public Private Partnership) for station fit-out, provision of rolling stock and rail systems, commissioning and operation of passenger services. Metrolink will require extensive deployment of Heavy Goods Vehicles (HGVs of all types from 3.5T to >12T) to support a wide range of activities, including deliveries, disposal and site servicing. Given the scale of operations, it is essential to ensure vehicle compliance with the European Union General Safety Regulations (EU GSR) from July 2024. A significant proportion of the HGV fleet in Ireland does not meet these standards, primarily due to manufacture and registration dates prior to July 2024. Although there is no national legal requirement to retrofit legacy vehicles within the Irish fleet, deploying large numbers of HGVs that are not fitted with the latest vehicle safety technology represents a significant hazard to vulnerable road users (both workforce and the general public). This presents an unacceptable risk to the programme which seeks a zero-tolerance approach to vehicle safety, to protect vulnerable road users both on and off various construction sites, zones and public roads. Metrolink and Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII) have identified three key vehicle safety systems that must be adopted on HGVs in use across the programme, to significantly reduce risks to vulnerable road users and improve overall safety across project sites: • Reversing Detection (RD) • Blind Side Information Systems (BSIS) • Moving Off Information Systems (MOIS) EU Regulation 2019/2144, the General Safety Regulation (GSR), sets mandatory standards for vehicle safety by requiring new vehicles to have advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) and meet specific performance criteria. From 2024 all new HGV (N2/N3) must have the following fitted as standard: • Intelligent Speed Assistance • Blind Spot Information System • Advanced Emergency Breaking System • Reversing Detection • Moving Off Information System • Tyre Pressure Monitoring System • Alcohol Interlock Installation Facilitation • Driver Drowsiness and Attention Warning

Procedure title: Tender for the Design, Supply and Installation of a Water Treatment System at Medite Europe DAC ‘26
Description: MEDITE Europe DAC has plans to modernize their MDF facility with an investment in new plan and equipment collectively called Project Shine. Project Shine involves the installation of the following: • Wet fuel handling system. • Dry Fuel handling system. • 56MW Biomass Energy. • MDF dryers. • Services + utilities to the above, mainly: o Compressed air o Water treatment systems o Fire detection + suppression o Natural Gas o Steam o Storm and foul water o Bunds where necessary Project Shine is shortly commencing the construction phase of the project and proposals are sought for the supply of Water Treatment System to supply process water at the correct specification to all consumers. Current Setup MEDITE’S current water distribution process flow diagram can be seen in Appendix 3. Water is drawn from the adjacent Anner River into the onsite settling ponds. These ponds serve both as site fire water and process water requirements. This water is then fed through a 7 cartridge 50-micron filter media. From the filter bank it passes through two parallel plate heat exchangers and then fed to various processes one of these being a water tank. From the water storage tank it is then pumped through a typical De-Alk and softener process and then feeds the existing Line 1 boilers and Line 2 energy plant. Scope of work The condition and age of the existing system presents challenges for future requirements in relation to Project Shine. The main areas of concern with the current system are: • Valve and pneumatic manifold obsolescence. • Instrumentation and automation obsolescence. • Maintainability. The scope of work for the water treatment system are as follows (relevant information can be found in Appendix 3): • Design + installation of a water treatment system to: • Deliver 30m3/hr of water, to the required specification, for the new energy plant + steam generator. • Deliver 15m3/hr of water, to the required specification, for the existing energy plant. • Be modular in design with capability of addition capacity. • Fully automated with local and remote-control functionality. • Remote + local SCADA ability. • Design to incorporate existing multi media filter and associated pumps. • Proposed location of skid unit shown in appendices. • Design + installation complies with the EU Machinery Directives. • Ensure if any HAZOP recommendations are identified are implemented. • Provide all necessary Safety File information to the PSDP. • Comply with the PSCS. • Ensure all contractors conform to Medite Policies where applicable i.e. no smoking, LOTO, Hot Works, Work at Heights. • Provide details of annual operational running cost in terms of; • Chemical usage if any. • Salt usage if any. • Typical wastewater quantities + constituents from backwash. • Typical energy costs. • Compressed air consumption. • Recommended Spare Parts Package. • 5 year After Sales Service Package to include: • Planned Preventative Maintenance Program. • Chemical supply, storage and offloading. • Salt supply if required. • Regular testing + adjusting to ensure required water quality + quantity is maintained. • Necessary reports. • Training. Medite have attempted to interpret the system requirements. Since the Supplier is an expert in the field of water treatment, the Supplier is asked to advise Medite of suitable equipment/systems and its requirements that are not fulfilled and to provide an option price for same. ** Please see the attached Tender Document for the full and complete scope of works and drawings **

Title: Ireland – Construction work for bridges and tunnels, shafts and subways – MetroLink, Dublin – Design and build civil infrastructure contract packages for the M401 and M402 contracts
Procedure title: MetroLink, Dublin – Design and build civil infrastructure contract packages for the M401 and M402 contracts
Description: The M401 and M402 (the M400 Contracts) will provide the civil engineering and infrastructure works for the MetroLink project, with each contract including the track alignment preparation, stations and structures including bridges and tunnels. The scope of the M400 Contracts is expected to comprise of the following: 1. Southern Section M401 – Charlemont to Northwood: • Bored railway tunnels, tunnel portals, evacuation / intervention shafts and ventilation shafts. • Below ground station excavations at Charlemont, St Stephen’s Green, Tara Station, O’Connell, Mater, Glasnevin, Griffith Park, Collins Avenue, Ballymun, Northwood up to 35 m deep including shell and core structures. • Required ancillary civil and accommodation works. 2. Northern Section M402 ­ Northwood to Estuary: • M50 viaduct, surface route (retained cut, cut and cover) and at­grade sections. • Broadmeadow river viaduct. • Estuary Station Park and Ride Facility (bulk earthworks and site preparation). • Preparation of the Dardistown Depot site and access road. • Bored tunnels and portals, evacuation / intervention shafts. • Stations excavations and associated logistics including Dardistown, Fosterstown, Swords Central, Seatown and Estuary. • It is currently anticipated that the construction of the underground MetroLink station at Dublin Airport will not be included in the M402 contract package and will be separately procured under the M120 Heavy Civils Enabling Works Framework. The Contracting Authority reserves the right at its discretion to include this work in the scope of the M402 contract. The procurement process for the M400 Contracts will be managed by TII, acting as the Contracting Authority, who will be the sole point of contact for Applicants. The procurement of the M400 Contracts (the Competition) will be conducted using the negotiated procedure with prior call for competition, Regulation 46 of the European Union (Award of Contracts by Utility Undertakings) Regulations 2016 (S.I. 286/2016). The Competition will consist of two lots; Lot 1: M401 contract and Lot 2: M402 contract. Applicants may apply for one or both lots, but can only be awarded one contract. The Competition will comprise two main stages: a prequalification stage with shortlisting at the end, and a tender stage, The prequalification stage will assess Applicants separately for each lot (M401 and M402) based on defined selection criteria for each lot, such as financial stability, technical capability, and relevant experience. The prequalification stage will commence with the Contracting Authority publishing a Pre­Qualification Questionnaire (PQQ). Provided that there is a sufficient number of Applicants for each lot, three Applicants for each lot will be shortlisted. TII reserves the right at its absolute discretion to shortlist the fourth highest ranked Applicant for one or both of the M400 Contracts. If less than three Applicants meet the minimum requirements for a lot, TII reserves the right to proceed with those Applicants to the second stage of the procurement for that lot. If shortlisted for both lots, Applicants may tender for both lots but can only be awarded one contract. The prequalification stage for the M400 Contracts will run concurrently and the tender stage for each contract will be staggered, with the M401 contract tender stage commencing first followed by the M402 contract tender stage. The tender stage may involve multiple stages, and the Contracting Authority reserves the right to include negotiation with Applicants. For each lot, the tender stage will commence with the Contracting Authority issuing the Invitation To Negotiate (ITN) to each shortlisted Applicant for that lot. The ITN will supersede the PQQ document and will contain the draft contract documents and specification. Detailed information regarding the award process and award criteria for the M400 Contracts will be included in the ITN for each lot. Applicants will then submit their tenders, which will be evaluated on Compliance, Quality and Cost criteria. The process may include negotiations to refine proposals and optimise commercial terms. The Contracting Authority will conduct a final evaluation to select the most economically advantageous tender for each lot. The Contracting Authority has the right, at any time and without notice to, terminate the competition (or part of it), change the basis or procedures of the competition or procure the contract by other means, or to do any combination of the aforementioned or anything else deemed appropriate. In line with the Irish Government’s climate action legislation and MetroLink’s sustainability and carbon management commitments outlined in the Railway Order, the M400 Contracts will include a structured framework for managing carbon performance to ensure alignment with carbon targets, including financial mechanisms to reward carbon performance. This approach aims to encourage innovation in low­carbon construction methods, materials, and logistics, and will form part of the overall contract performance assessment.

Title: Ireland – Weather stations – Integrated Meteorological and Eddy Covariance Stations
Procedure title: Integrated Meteorological and Eddy Covariance Stations
Description: Tenders are sought for the Supply and Delivery, of three (3) Integrated Meteorological and Eddy Covariance Stations for Trinity College Dublin (TCD). This equipment is intended to support high-quality measurement of ecosystem–atmosphere exchanges under Irish environmental conditions. The systems must provide robust, high frequency measurements of CO₂, H₂O, wind components, radiation, air temperature, and humidity, with reliable data acquisition, storage, processing, and real-time remote access. The EC stations will support undergraduate and postgraduate laboratory experiments and student-led project work, while also enhancing long-term research capacity in environmental monitoring, greenhouse gas fluxes, and climate–ecosystem interactions.

Description: Lot 1: Provide civil engineering services to support the maintenance of the existing fibre network infrastructure and assist with the design and construction of new customer connections and network extensions as required. The scope includes both planned and emergency works, ensuring compliance with all relevant standards and regulations. Lot 2: Provide comprehensive network design and surveying services to support the deployment of fibre infrastructure Lot 3: Provide comprehensive GIS Design and Asset Management System services to support the deployment of fibre infrastructure. The scope includes, but is not limited to:

Title: Ireland – Telecommunications services – Prior Information Notice for International Subsea Telecommunications Connectivity Programme
Procedure title: Prior Information Notice for International Subsea Telecommunications Connectivity Programme
Description: The Department of Culture, Communications and Sport (DCCS) wishes to inform the market that it intends to progress a procurement process relating to the development of international subsea telecommunications connectivity. This supports the Government of Ireland’s intent to ensure the security and resilience of our digital infrastructure across our networks and sub-sea cable infrastructure, as announced in the recently published National Digital and AI Strategy 2030 (“Digital Ireland: Connecting our People, Securing our Future”). DCCS will undertake a structured supply chain and market engagement process over the coming months to help shape the final procurement approach, with the intention of issuing the tender within 12 months. The development aims to ensure direct and robust subsea fibre connectivity between Ireland and Mainland Europe on an ongoing basis to 2050, with an adequate level of redundancy and diversity. The main objective is to diversify Ireland’s international subsea telecommunications connectivity and in particular to enable the delivery of at least two new subsea cable routes from Ireland to Northern Europe with delivery of the first route commencing by circa 2031. Interested parties are encouraged to: • Monitor eTenders and ensure the appropriate CPV codes are selected so that notifications relating to this engagement are received. • Await further details on upcoming supplier briefings, market engagement activities, and the release of formal documentation will follow. • Begin considering any potential solutions, innovations, efficiencies, or value adding approaches they may wish to bring forward during the procurement process. DCCS anticipates active engagement with industry throughout this phase. Input from the market will be used to inform the design of the procurement, enhance value for money, and support efficient and effective delivery of the overall programme. This notice provides potential bidders with an overview of DCCS’s proposed intervention in Ireland’s international subsea telecommunications cable market. It outlines the programme objectives, the preferred intervention model, and expected future procurement activity. Subsea telecommunications cables carry approximately 99% of global data traffic and are essential for Ireland’s economic and digital infrastructure. As an island nation and a European technology hub, Ireland requires resilient, high capacity, and diverse subsea connections to support future demand and strengthen direct connectivity with EU Member States, and to provide for onward connectivity, through those new connections, to markets in Africa, Asia, and South America A Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case (PBC) have been completed in line with the Infrastructure Guidelines. These assessments concluded that a significant funding gap exists in the development of new subsea cable links between Ireland and the EU. Preferred Intervention Approach A range of State intervention options were considered. Following financial and economic appraisal, a hybrid intervention solution has been identified as the preferred approach. This hybrid solution includes: 1. Early-Stage Marine Survey Support: Upfront funding for marine surveys. This will facilitate detailed project design for the realisation of viable solutions. 2. Capital Grant Support and availability payment support for delivery of viable projects: This may be initiated as a second stage to bridge funding gaps and enable delivery for future projects. Forward Notice of Procurement Activity This briefing note serves as advance notification to the market that: • A procurement process for the initial subsea cable project (Early-Stage Marine Support) is expected to commence following Approval Gate 2. • Further procurements relating to additional subsea cable projects in accordance with 2 above may be initiated at a later date. Potential bidders are encouraged to monitor future DCCS publications and procurement portals for updates.

Title: Ireland – Research consultancy services – AFBI03-ITT03 Working at Height Expertise and Supervision
Procedure title: AFBI03-ITT03 Working at Height Expertise and Supervision
Description: The British Trust for Ornithology (BTO) and The Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB) are project partners in the ACCLIMATISE project, supported by PEACEPLUS, a programme managed by the Special EU Programmes Body (SEUPB). ACCLIMATISE is led by the Agri-Food and Biosciences Institute (AFBI). Within this project, BTO is leading Work Package 2: ‘Transboundary Conservation Strategies and Sustainable Management of Marine Predators’. RSPB and BTO are co-leading the ornithological work within the project; this specifically includes seabird tracking and diet analysis, at sea surveys, passive acoustic monitoring, and developing a transboundary seabird conservation strategy and action plans for priority threatened seabird species. BTO and RSPB are looking for suitably qualified and experienced companies to Tender for the provision of Working at Height (WAH) expertise as part of the ACCLIMATISE project between May and August 2026. BTO and RSPB staff are trained as Industrial Rope Access Techniques Association (IRATA) Level 1 Operatives and for each Lot in this Call for Tender (CfT) are seeking field supervision from IRATA certified technicians (Level 3 and Level 2). The work will be focused on facilitating access and supervising researchers at seabird colonies across Northern Ireland. Specifications for the work are split into two Lots, Lot 1, led by BTO and Lot 2, led by RSPB. In both cases, the work carried out by the Supplier will be the same, namely enabling the safe access of Level 1 trained BTO and RSPB staff to seabird colonies in coastal locations in Northern Ireland in order to catch birds for GPS tagging as part of the ACCLIMATISE project. The primary difference between the Lots is the location of work. In both cases, the first two weeks of catching work will be located on Rathlin Island (55.29238, -6.19234), where BTO and RSPB will be working as a single unit. However, for the final two weeks BTO and RSPB teams will be split, with RSPB continuing to work on Rathlin, and BTO moving on to colonies located in Portrush (55.19821, -6.67199) and Newcastle (54.18917, -5.87803). This will result in the contractor supplying IRATA Level 3 and Level 2 support on Rathlin to a single team at the start of the field season but once BTO leave the island, concurrent Level 3 and Level 2 support will also be necessary on the mainland.

Title: Ireland – Installation services of fire protection equipment – Tender for the Design, Supply and Installation of Fire Extinguishing (Suppression) Systems in 3 MCC Rooms at MEDITE Europe DAC ‘26
Procedure title: Tender for the Design, Supply and Installation of Fire Extinguishing (Suppression) Systems in 3 MCC Rooms at MEDITE Europe DAC ‘26
Description: MEDITE Europe DAC are looking for suitably qualified Fire suppression companies to install suppression systems in the following Motor Control Centre (MCC) rooms across the Medite plant. • Anner HV Sub-Station • Fire-Pump House MCC • Line1 post-press MCC Project Background Mandatory Insurance Requirement Medite electrical distribution network comprises 17 Motor Control Centre rooms, and the main HV Switch-room located at Anner Substation. (See MCC layout drawing in Appendix 3). A number of these MCCs and the main Switch-room are considered higher impact and risk, due to the criticality of the processes they support and the ageing condition of the installed switchgear and associated cooling systems. Overall Program Objectives The multi-year goal of this program is to ensure that all site MCC + HV switch-room comply with legislative requirements and industry best practice for extinguishing electrical fires automatically. It is proposed to install a similar Clean Agent gaseous suppression system with appropriate smoke detection in all MCC rooms, starting with those with critical switchgear. Program estimated to take ~4 years. The program scope includes: • Design of suppression system for each room considering:  Size and fabric of structure  Presence of a floor void(s) or not  Age + condition of switchgear (risk of overheating + fire)  Ability to seal room effectively *  Type of cooling + air-handling (AHU) in place  Characterization of pressure in room now – Positive or Negative **  Ability to locate pressurized cylinders nearby • All necessary civil, mechanical and electrical (pre)works to enable the chosen system(s) • Integration of each system’s controls into the existing plant fire alarm system, where applicable to deliver the project goals • Ensure compatibility of control system with existing ones (fire control panel) * for total flood systems ** most Medite MCCs are positive pressure to keep out dust As part of the 2026 program of works the following 3 electrical rooms are to be addressed: • Anner Sub-station switch-room • Fire Pumphouse MCC room • Line1 Press Outfeed MCC room Preferred route is to install an Inert Gas system with appropriate Smoke Detection system. Scope of Works • Evaluate Enclosure Integrity Test results (‘door-fan’ test report) • Determine existing baseline for cooling, air-handling + room pressure profile • Based on results of EIT report referenced in Appendix 3, recommend and execute remedial measures • Determine and design optimal suppression system • Design and specify all necessary smoke / heat detection systems • Fire seal room to appropriate fire-rate • Install fire detection system • Install suppression system • Link system to house alarm and test • Validate and certify finished system *** Please see the attached Tender Document for the full and Complete scope of Works ***

Title: Ireland – Buses and coaches – Annual Readvertisement of Qualification System for the Purchase and or Leasing of Buses and Coaches for Bus Éireann/Irish Bus - (Annual Readvertisement Publication Number 2/8)
Procedure title: Annual Readvertisement of Qualification System for the Purchase and or Leasing of Buses and Coaches for Bus Éireann/Irish Bus - (Annual Readvertisement Publication Number 2/8)
Description: Bus Éireann intends to procure low emission coaches and schools buses, and where possible zero-emission coaches with low environmental impact in compliance with the latest EURO VI Regulation. The vehicles will comply, as appropriate, with the EPA’s guidelines on road transport vehicles and the European Communities (Clean and Energy Efficient Road Transport Vehicles) (Amendment) Regulations 2021. To be considered for inclusion on a Qualification Panel(s), applicants must complete the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire (PQQ) providing relevant details in relation to the criteria set out below for assessment. It is envisaged that this qualification system will be used to either purchase and or lease during the five-year term of the Qualification System. Economic operators apply once to qualify onto the panel by providing details of their financial and technical capacity against predefined published Selection Criteria within a PQQ. The Qualification Panel for the Purchase and or Lease of Buses and Coaches will be broken down in to sub categories called Lot 1 – Purchase of Buses and Coaches, and Lot 2 – Lease of Buses and Coaches. Economic operators can apply for the Lot(s) that best reflect their commercial operations. Economic operators must complete a PQQ for the Lot(s) that they wish to qualify to. Only economic operators who satisfy the selection criteria of each individual Lot will qualify on to that Lot. After the initial advertisement, the panel must be advertised annually for the duration of the panel (5 years) to continually inform the market place of its existence. Economic Operators can apply to qualify on to the panel, throughout the duration of the panel. Economic Operators who are already qualified to the panel can also amend their application at any interval should their financial or technical capacity or capability change. Qualifying onto a panel does not guarantee any work and/or contracts to a supplier. There is no obligation to use the Qualification Panel and contracts can be advertised on an individual basis using the Negotiated Procedure. (Annual Republication Number 2/8)
